scope_note: Adversarial corrective synthesis for the Microsoft MWH campus in Quincy. Four estimates add distinct real-property account 72793 and personal-property account 84139 base-paid amounts once for each complete matching tax year, 2022-2025. A fifth estimate states only the 2025 same-account-scope annual public-service-cost break-even identity authorized by study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Every estimate remains unallocated to the selected 143,439-square-foot IM3 footprint. Incomplete 2026 personal tax, other Microsoft accounts, state incentives, utility charges, Oxford infrastructure outlays and actual public-service costs are excluded, so no net fiscal result is asserted.

estimates.decision_relevance: Provides a reproducible annual MWH campus property-tax contribution without allocating the accounts to the selected building or mixing broader regional tax claims.

assumptions: Accounts 72793 and 84139 are distinct real- and personal-property accounts for the same MWH site.
The two source claims cover the same tax year and both balances are fully paid.
No other Microsoft account, estimated-tax table, incentive, utility amount or public cost is added or subtracted.

limitations: This is an account-level aggregation, not an audited government-wide receipt or net benefit.
The campus accounts are unallocated to the selected building and may not include every tenant account.

estimates.label: 2025 MWH two-account annual local service-cost break-even threshold

period.label: Grant County tax year 2025 equal-cost threshold for fully paid statements 57524 and 61472

scope.label: Microsoft MWH real account 72793 plus personal account 84139 at 1515 NW Port Industrial Parkway across their local taxing recipients

interval.interpretation: The threshold equals the exact same-year two-account paid-tax aggregation by definition; it is not an estimate of actual public cost.

parameters.name: real_property_tax_paid
parameters.transformation: Included once in the equal-cost threshold

parameters.name: personal_property_tax_paid
parameters.transformation: Included once in the equal-cost threshold

estimates.confidence_rationale: The two payment inputs and threshold identity are exact, while recipient cash reconciliation and actual same-scope marginal service and infrastructure costs remain unavailable.
estimates.decision_relevance: States the annual local public-cost level that would exactly offset the latest complete MWH paid-tax base without fabricating costs or claiming a fiscal surplus.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Annual marginal fire, police, road, water, wastewater, administrative, infrastructure and financing costs aligned to accounts 72793 and 84139, recipient jurisdictions and tax year 2025

derivation.formula: same-scope annual marginal public-service cost at break-even = $4,728,047.25 real paid + $9,106,834.90 personal paid = $13,834,882.15
assumptions: The threshold is an identity, not an observed or estimated public cost.
The hypothetical cost threshold uses the same two accounts and tax-year scope as the companion paid-tax aggregation.
Fund 450 outlays, the $31 million reuse-system cost, bonds, state incentives, utility charges and incomplete 2026 payments are excluded because their periods or incidence do not match.
No positive or negative fiscal margin is asserted without observed same-scope costs.

limitations: This is not an estimate of actual public-service cost.
The input is an account-level paid-tax aggregation, not an audited recipient revenue ledger.
The campus accounts are unallocated to the selected inventory building and may omit tenant property.
A fiscal margin is positive only if actual same-scope marginal costs are below this threshold and negative only if they are above it; neither condition is established.
estimates.notes: Policy-authorized equal-cost identity only. Do not sum this threshold with the tax contribution or present it as a cost, subsidy or net fiscal result.
